manifest.name: @local/dsh-model-toggle
manifest.description: Per-model and per-provider enable/disable switches, plus third-party thinking-effort rules, for the DeepSeek Harness desktop app (profile bundle carrying host and web-client halves; app.asar untouched).

readme.text: Two missing controls for the **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** desktop app, delivered entirely through DSH's own extension mechanisms — the signed `app.asar` is never modified.

1. **Per-model and per-provider enable/disable switches** on the **Settings → Models** page. A disabled model disappears from the composer's bottom-right model selector (and the `/model` palette), while its configuration is kept intact and can be re-enabled at any time.
2. **Thinking-effort levels for third-party providers.** Custom `baseURL` providers normally get no effort selector because nothing declares `reasoningEfforts` for them. A layered rule set — keyed on model-id / API protocol / `baseURL` regex, exactly like ZCode's rule table — writes the native `reasoningEfforts` / `compat` fields back into the provider's own settings.

A plugin panel inside each provider card on the **Settings → Models** page:

```
┌ Settings → Models ───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  myrouter-ds  [custom]  ●                    [Edit] [Delete]      │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  API key / custom settings (base URL, protocol, …)         │   │

- **Where:** a block rendered by the plugin's client half into the Models page's own `settings.models.provider-card` slot — the page bundle itself is untouched.
- **Provider master switch:** enables/disables every model of that provider at once.
- **Per-model switch:** one row per model; a switch that is off hides the model from the selector while keeping its configuration.
- **Trade-off:** model rows expose no extension slot, so the switches live in this panel rather than inline on each model row.

| Platform | Status |
| --- | --- |
| **macOS** | ✅ Built, installed and verified on macOS (DSH desktop, Electron). This is the reference platform. |
| **Windows** | ⚠️ Adapted but **not tested**. The tools now resolve the home directory via `os.homedir()` (so `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop` works), use `os.tmpdir()` for scratch, and auto-probe the usual `app.asar` locations under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\…` / `%ProgramFiles%`. If detection misses, pass `--asar <path>` explicitly. |
| **Linux** | ⚠️ Adapted but **not tested**. Same story: `app.asar` candidates under `/opt`, `/usr/lib`, `/usr/share`, `~/.local/share`. Use `--asar <path>` if none match. |

The plugin code itself (`lib/`) is plain JavaScript running inside DSH's own runtime and is platform-independent. What is platform-specific is only **path discovery** in the tools, which is why the tools take `--profile` and `--asar` overrides.

> Please report your platform if you get it running elsewhere — the anchor-based page patcher is the only part that can break across DSH versions, and it fails loudly rather than writing a half-patched file.

| Part | Location | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bundle `@local/dsh-model-toggle` | profile manifest dependency (`link:`) + `dsh.profile.bundles` | One package, two halves. The manifest entry is what makes it appear in Settings → Plugins, where the Plugin Manager enables/disables it. |
| Host half `lib/index.js` | same package | Owns the settings namespace `model-toggle` (`disabled: ["provider/model"]`, volatile → persisted into the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`). Narrowly wraps `sessionController.modelCatalog()` to drop disabled models from the selector's only data source, and runs the thinking-effort rule reconciler. |
| Client half `lib/client.js` | same package, `dsh.client` + `exports["./client"]` | A `window.__ModuleLoader__` bundle that registers the panel into `settings.models.provider-card`. Reads and writes `disabled` through `ctx.configForms.get("model-toggle")` and reads each provider's `models` from `configForms.describe()`. Registers only while the namespace is served, so disabling the plugin leaves no trace. |
| Bundle patch `cordis.patch.yml` | same package | Inserts the `model-toggle` row. The profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` keeps only the saved settings override.

Nothing in `app.asar` is touched, so the code signature and `ElectronAsarIntegrity` stay valid. The loader composes bundle layers at process start and caches client-module metadata, so **one DSH restart is required after installing or changing the client half**; after that, enabling/disabling the plugin in Settings → Plugins is live.

The plugin is a profile **bundle**. `manage.mjs` registers it; the Plugin Manager owns it afterwards.

```sh
cd dsh-model-controls
node tools/manage.mjs status          # what is currently installed
node tools/manage.mjs install         # link dependency + bundle selection + symlink

```

After the restart, **Settings → Plugins** lists `@local/dsh-model-toggle`: toggle it there. Disabling removes the host half and the panel together; enabling restores both, with no restart. The saved switch states live in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and survive either way.

Uninstall / roll back:sh
node tools/manage.mjs uninstall       # remove the link dependency and bundle selection
```

`manage.mjs` backs up the profile manifest before writing, and on upgrade from an older install it removes the legacy hand-written `insert:` block from `cordis.patch.yml` while keeping the saved settings. The old whole-page route is deprecated but kept for rollback: `node tools/patch-page.mjs check|install|revert`.
```yaml

readme.section: the config of the model-toggle entry in cordis.patch.yml
readme.text:
rules:                                  # evaluated in order; later rules override field by field
  - match: { provider: "^myrouter-grok$" }
    levels: [off, low, medium, high]
    map: { off: null, low: low, medium: medium, high: high }
  - match: { baseUrl: "api\\.example\\.com" }   # match the provider site
    levels: [off, high]
    map: { off: null, high: high }              # off = send nothing; high = send "high"
    compat: { thinkingFormat: deepseek }        # optional: pin the wire field family
overrides:                              # per-model spec, highest priority
  "myrouter/deepseek-v4.1-flash": { levels: [off, medium], map: { off: null, medium: medium } }
fallback: false                         # what unmatched models get; false = no effort row at all
```

readme.section: the config of the model-toggle entry in cordis.patch.yml
readme.text:
- `match`: `provider` / `model` / `api` / `baseUrl`, all regexes, all must match; an omitted key means "any".
- `levels` + `map`: levels missing from `map` fall back to a same-named wire value; `off` maps to `null` (= send nothing) by default. You can also write `efforts: { off: null, high: high }` directly.
- `compat`: optional, merged by key. The available keys are the ones the adapter exposes (`thinkingFormat`, `supportsReasoningEffort`, `supportsThinkingTokenBudget`, `thinkingTokenBudgetField`, `maxTokensField`, …). A key the protocol does not accept is reported as an error by `llm-pi-ai`.yaml
fallback: { levels: [off, high], map: { off: null, high: high }, compat: { supportsReasoningEffort: false } }
```

readme.section: Field ownership ("what you edit by hand stops following the rules")
readme.text: Rule output lands in the same configuration layer as the user's own edits in the Models page, so the plugin records what it wrote in `model-toggle.managed`:

readme.section: Field ownership ("what you edit by hand stops following the rules")
readme.text:
- The user layer has no such field and the plugin never wrote it → the rule fills it.
- The user layer's value **equals** what the plugin last wrote → still the plugin's; it keeps following rule updates.
- The user layer's value **differs** (hand-edited) → the field is released; rules never touch it again (mirroring ZCode's *"When you manually change a setting, that setting becomes manually managed"*).
- The plugin's value was deleted → also treated as a hand edit, released.
- A rule stops declaring a field (e.g. the rule was deleted) → the plugin clears the value it wrote and leaves no ownership record, so re-adding the rule can take over again.

readme.section: Field ownership ("what you edit by hand stops following the rules")
readme.text: `compat` is owned **per key**: when the Models page writes back it also returns schema defaults (`chatTemplateKwargs`, `chatTemplateArgs`, …); those extra keys do not count as hand edits, and rules keep managing only their own keys.

**Verified offline by capturing the real request bodies:** on an `openai-completions` route, adding rules is **lazy** — with no level selected the request body is byte-identical to before, and only a selected level adds `reasoning_effort`. On an `openai-responses` route it is *not* lazy: once a model declares levels, pi-ai sends `reasoning: { effort: "none" }` even with no level selected (the predicate is `thinkingLevelMap.off !== null`, and DSH's `off: null` parses as "key absent"). Decide accordingly before enabling rules on Responses routes.
```sh

readme.section: full rollback to before the rules were added (including the plugin's written-back fields)
readme.text:
cp ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml.bak-before-reasoning-rules-<timestamp> \
   ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml
```

Deleting a single `rules:` entry is enough for the plugin to clean up the `reasoningEfforts` it wrote for that provider on its next reconcile. To just stop using a level for one model, pick "provider default" / "off" in the selector — no config edit needed.

readme.section: full rollback to before the rules were added (including the plugin's written-back fields)
readme.text: Note that the write-back happens on the **next catalog read** (opening the model selector, or restarting DSH): the plugin must write first to record ownership; if you hand-write those fields beforehand they are treated as manual edits and permanently released.

The plugin lives in the profile, so replacing the app bundle leaves it in place, but the extensions it relies on can change:

- If the internal seams it uses (`modelCatalog`, `configForms`, `settings`, the `settings.models.provider-card` slot) changed, the entry fails to activate and the features are gone until adapted.
- The client half is plain JavaScript served from the package; only the slot name and the client service names are API surface.

```sh
node tools/manage.mjs install         # re-link / re-select after a profile reinstall
```

Back up `cordis.patch.yml` before updating — your switch states live there.

```sh
node tools/test-manage.mjs                          # 14/14 installer: link + bundle + saved settings, idempotent, clean uninstall
node tools/test-rules.mjs                           # 55/55 rule logic: matching, layering, validation, ownership/release, idempotency
node --expose-internals tools/verify-rules.mjs      # 17/17 end-to-end in an isolated profile on a booted packaged runtime
node tools/patch-page.mjs check                     # legacy whole-page patcher (deprecated; kept for rollback)

`verify-rules.mjs` and `probe-request-body.mjs` need the app's runtime tree on disk (default `<tmpdir>/dsh-test/runtime2`, override with `DSH_TEST_RUNTIME`). Build it once, read-only, straight out of the packaged app:

```sh
node tools/extract-runtime.mjs          # ~317 MiB of @deepseek-ai/* + bundled deps
node --expose-internals tools/verify-rules.mjs        # 17/17
node --expose-internals tools/probe-request-body.mjs <patch-file> high
```

`--asar <path>` points at a non-standard install; `--out <dir>` / `--only <prefix>` / `--list` control what is copied. Nothing is ever written back into the archive.

`probe-request-body.mjs <patch> [level]` boots a real provider config offline with `fetch` stubbed and prints the exact JSON each model would send with and without a selected level — no network, fake key. Run it before adding rules to see whether they change the default request body.

Also verified: the client bundle materializes and its `apply(ctx)` registers the panel into `settings.models.provider-card` and renders the provider's models; the package declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and `dsh.client`; and the bundle composes into exactly one `model-toggle` row with the saved settings applied (`dsh --profile <copy> --dump-config`).

- Requires one DSH restart after installing or changing the client half; after that, enabling/disabling the plugin in Settings → Plugins is live. No page re-patching on DSH updates.
- The switches live in a panel inside each provider card, not inline on each model row — model rows expose no extension slot.
- Switches are offered only for providers that **declare models in their settings** (the model list comes from the settings document).
- The effort rule layer likewise only manages providers that declare a `models` list — routes that rely purely on pi-ai's built-in catalog are left alone (otherwise the built-in catalog would be frozen into the user config).
- Write-back replaces the whole `models` array (the settings API replaces arrays as a unit). For providers whose models are already declared in the user config this just adds fields.
- `defaultEffort` (the level pre-selected when a model is picked) is not wired: in DSH that is the route-level `reasoning`, and filling it in would affect the whole provider. The default stays "provider default" (no field sent); you pick a level yourself.
- Disabling the model the current session is using leaves the composer unusable until you pic

```
lib/index.js       host half: settings namespace, catalog filter, reconciler entry
lib/rules.js       rule layer: matching, spec parsing, ownership planning
lib/client.js      client half: the in-page panel registered into settings.models.provider-card
cordis.patch.yml   bundle patch: inserts the model-toggle row

The thinking-effort scheme is modelled on **[zai-org/ZCode](https://github.com/zai-org/ZCode)** (Apache-2.0): ordered level lists plus a level→wire mapping, resolved through layered rules keyed on model id / API type / base URL, with per-model user-editable specs. `docs/zcode-reasoning-effort.md` records what was examined (branch `main` @ `29628c9a`).
